title: Circuit Condensation: Train the Circuit Smaller
hook: Circuit discovery on a frozen model returns hundreds of edges nobody can check. Post-train the model to route the behavior through fewer, and circuits shrink 8x on average — up to 316x.
key_points: Circuit Condensation post-trains models to concentrate behaviors into smaller causal graphs.
Each round prunes low-attribution edges and trains a low-rank adapter to match the original through what remains.
A cut is kept only if task performance and general capability survive.
Across four behaviors and eight models, condensed circuits are smaller than the strongest frozen baseline in 30 of 32 settings — 8.1x on average, up to 316x.

content_html: Mechanistic interpretability explains behavior through circuits: the components and connections that carry it. The practical problem is size. Discovery on a frozen model routinely returns hundreds of edges — too many to inspect by hand, compare across models, or verify exhaustively. Senthil Kumar proposes changing the model instead of the search.
extra_html:
The method

Circuit Condensation post-trains a model to concentrate a behavior into a smaller causal graph. Each round prunes low-attribution edges and trains a low-rank adapter to match the original model's behavior through whatever remains. A cut is retained only if both task performance and general capability survive, so the model is not being lobotomized into a narrow specialist.

Results

Across four behaviors and eight models, condensed circuits beat the strongest frozen baseline in 30 of 32 settings — 8.1x smaller on average, up to 316x. The control matters: rerunning the same search without weight updates gives larger circuits in 29 of 32 settings, so the reduction comes from reshaping the model, not from a better search.

On indirect object identification, the classic interpretability testbed, condensation isolates 24 heads, 17 of them with documented roles, versus 61 heads and 36 undocumented ones for the matched frozen circuit. Testing every subset of 19 circuits finds 11 that cannot be reduced further and reveals removable edges in the rest.

The caveats worth keeping

A condensed circuit is a sufficient sub-circuit of the published mechanism, not a reconstruction of it — you have made the model simpler, not discovered that it was simple. And pair ablations expose dependencies between edges, confirming that their effects cannot be understood independently.

flashcards.prompt: What does Circuit Condensation change that ordinary circuit discovery does not?
flashcards.back_html: The weights. Discovery searches a frozen model for the edges carrying a behavior; condensation post-trains the model so the behavior runs through fewer edges in the first place.

flashcards.prompt: What is the important caveat about a condensed circuit?
flashcards.back_html: It is a sufficient sub-circuit of the published mechanism, not a reconstruction of it — and pair ablations show edges depend on each other, so effects cannot be read off individually.
